notes:
Pipeline (scripts in https://github.com/m0etez/subway-builder-grand-tunis):

1. Residents: WorldPop 2020 constrained 100 m population grid (total population), rescaled per governorate so totals match the 2024 census (RGPH 2024, INS Tunisie: Tunis 1,075,306; Ariana 668,552; Ben Arous 722,828; La Manouba 418,354). The only official areas are the governorates; the 100 m distribution comes from WorldPop's model. Commuting residents = 34% employment ratio (national employed population is 30.8% per RGPH 2024, Greater Tunis is above average) + 5% school trips.
2. Jobs: no geocoded official employment data exists for Tunisia. Total jobs = employed residents. 75% are spread with weights from OpenStreetMap features (land-use areas with per-hectare densities, office/government/commercial building footprints x levels, shops, hospitals, schools, hotels, markets, airport terminal); 25% are population-proportional local jobs.
3. Points: H3 res-9 cells (res-8 where activity is low), activity-weighted centroids.
4. Flows: doubly-constrained gravity model, home-work exp(-0.16 d) and home-school exp(-0.7 d) on network-scaled distance; discretised into groups of 50. No commute-flow data is used.
5. Special demand via depot add_points: Tunis-Carthage airport (12k/day), 10 university hubs (~121k student trips), Medina souks, malls, beaches, heritage sites, Radès stadium, La Goulette port, Bab Saâdoun hospitals.
6. Driving times: local OSRM on the OSM network, x1.6 peak-hour congestion factor.

Placement notes (nearest dropdown options chosen, please reclassify if needed): jobs are placed on OSM building footprints by type (office/government/commercial/retail/industrial x levels) plus OSM land-use areas and POIs with assumed per-type densities. People are placed by WorldPop's constrained model (population only in settled cells derived from building footprints, weighted by covariates), not by per-building dwelling counts.

Data vintages: WorldPop 2020, RGPH 2024, OSM extract of 2026-11-16.
